criteria.evidence: All five detailed-stage sections plus Agent intent (ICE) are present and substantive, e.g. Benefit hypothesis gives who ('the plan owner, who plans work toward a business intent'), belief ('work can start before the model is complete, if the model links its parts by these rules') and proof ('a ready check gives one answer for each capability and functionality'); Boundary has In/Out/Never lines; four guiding rules; four linked functionalities.

Edges and rules carry their reason: 'In: search by domain... Domains do not decide when work starts, so search is their only job.'; 'Never: change how model pages are saved. Every play already writes pages that way, and a change would break them.'; 'Old pages still pass. A gap in a page made before these rules is a warning, not an error. A new rule must not break an old model.'; Out lines name the owner: 'The plan capabilities own this (Build a plan, View plans, Manage a plan).' The one open point is flagged openly: '(Our proposal: what counts as a gap is not yet agreed.)'

Every section is discrete bullets, one point each; functionalities state behaviour, not user stories: 'Ready without a domain (fn-724): the ready check gives its answer without the domain.'; ICE lines each start with one of the six labels ('Goal:', 'Limit:', 'Fails if:', 'Context:', 'Checked by:', 'Quality need:').
No parent doc supplied ('parent doc: none').

A cold reader can state the what ('a ready check gives one answer... Ready / Partly ready / Not ready'), the why ('work can start before the model is complete') and the edges ('Out: making, showing or changing a plan'; 'Never: stop a write... the page is always kept'). Terms are defined inline: business intent ('a goal a person sets for the product'), needs ('the other one must be done first'), identified by ('That link is history, not an order of work'). Minor residue only in the agent-facing ICE ('exists in the spine', 'pre-v5 model page'), which the person-facing sections already explain in plain words ('Old pages still pass').
